title: Guardrails and Journeys Hub: Core Controls and Operational Playbooks
author: Asha Menon
content:
Summary

This page is the company-wide reference for core operational guardrails and common workflows (Access & Permissions, Change Management, Data Management, Procurement & Expenses, Vendor Management, Travel policy, and internal templates). It consolidates decision criteria, approval thresholds, roles, and step-by-step procedures so teams can operate consistently while enabling rapid product delivery. Use this hub as the canonical source for operational patterns; for team-specific deviations request an exception (see Governance & Exceptions).

Scope

- Applies to all Redwood Inference employees, contractors, and approved vendors.
- Covers cross-functional processes that impact security, finance, or customer data.
- Does not replace product-team implementation guides; it standardizes approvals, controls, and handoffs.

Principles

1. Least privilege by default: grant only the access necessary for a defined task and duration.
2. Clear separation of duties: custody (people who operate) vs. control (people who approve).
3. Risk-based approvals: higher risk requires more stringent approval paths.
4. Auditability and traceability: all requests must be recorded in the authoritative workflow system.
5. Continuous improvement: metrics collected for bottlenecks and policy tuning.

Key Roles and Owners

- Requestor: the employee initiating an action (access request, change, purchase, travel).
- Approver: person with delegated authority to approve based on thresholds (manager, finance approver, security reviewer).
- Owner Team: team responsible for operating a service or dataset (documented in service catalog).
- Control Owner: centralized team accountable for the policy (Finance & Legal for procurement; Security for access; Data Governance for data policies).
- Approvals Admin: platform team that maintains forms and workflows (IT/Platform).

Access and Permissions

Overview
- Access is managed centrally via the identity provider (IdP) and group memberships. Privileged access (production, PII datasets, KMS) requires additional approvals and periodic recertification.

Access Tiers and Approval Requirements

| Tier | Target Resources | Approval Path | Duration | Recertification |
|------|------------------|---------------|----------|----------------|
| Tier 1 (Standard) | Corporate apps (email, wiki, Slack) | Manager | 1 year auto-expiry | Annual manager recert |
| Tier 2 (Privileged) | Production consoles, deploy pipelines | Manager + Service Owner | 90 days | Quarterly recert by service owner |
| Tier 3 (Sensitive) | PII datasets, KMS, private customer environments | Manager + Service Owner + Security | 30 days | Monthly recert + audit |

Request Workflow (Access)

1. Requestor opens the Access Request form in the IT portal and selects resource and tier.
2. Automated checks run (manager mapping, MFA status, current memberships).
3. Approver(s) review in-place; approvers must add justification when granting Tier 2/3.
4. Provisioning webhook updates group membership in IdP; provisioning logs appended to audit store.
5. Expiry reminder sent 14 days before expiration; auto-remediate if not recertified.

Change Management

Purpose
- Ensure safe, auditable changes to production systems while enabling rapid delivery. Changes are categorized by risk and must follow an approval and rollout plan.

Change Categories and Gates

- Standard Change: low-risk, pre-authorized (e.g., routine config tweaks, security patching windows).
- Minor Change: single-service change; requires Service Owner sign-off and smoke tests.
- Major Change: cross-service or customer-impacting; requires Change Advisory Board (CAB) review and rollback plan.
- Emergency Change: must follow Emergency CAB retrospective within 48 hours.

Change Process (high level)

1. Create change ticket with description, scope, rollout plan, backout procedure, monitoring plan, and owner.
2. Automated risk scoring computes initial category (based on blast radius, data sensitivity, customer impact).
3. If Major, schedule CAB and notify stakeholders; Minor and Standard follow simplified approval.
4. Execute in an approved window; monitor metrics and error budgets.
5. Complete post-deploy checklist and link to deployment artifact.

Data Management

Guiding Policies
- Data classification: All data must be labeled (Public, Internal, Confidential, Restricted).
- Data access control maps to classification. Sensitive or Restricted data requires explicit data access request and auditing.
- Backups and retention schedules are defined per dataset owner.

Data Handling Checklist

- Verify classification and legal constraints.
- Ensure encryption at-rest and in-transit for Confidential/Restricted.
- Confirm retention policy and data deletion process.
- Log access and set alerts for anomalous access patterns.

Procurement & Expenses

Purchase Thresholds and Approvals

| Amount (USD) | Approval Required | Procurement Involvement |
|--------------|-------------------|------------------------|
| <= 1,000 | Manager | No vendor setup required |
| 1,001 - 25,000 | Manager + Finance Approver | Procurement validates T&Cs |
| > 25,000 | Manager + Finance Director + Legal | Procurement-led RFP / Contract review |

Preferred Procurement Flow

1. Use the Purchase Request template in the approvals system.
2. Attach quotes, justification, and budget code.
3. Procurement validates vendor, tax status, and standard contract requirements.
4. Finance issues PO; vendor onboarding collects W-9 / VAT details and security questionnaire as applicable.

Expense Policy Highlights

- Employees must submit expenses within 30 days with receipts.
- Travel per-diem follows published bands; exceptions require manager + finance sign-off.
- Corporate cards are issued on manager recommendation and subject to monthly reconciliation.

Vendor Management

Onboarding Steps

1. Requestor raises Vendor Onboarding ticket with scope and contact.
2. Procurement runs vendor risk classification (Low/Medium/High).
3. High-risk vendors require security questionnaire, SOC report, and legal review.
4. Contract sign-off tracked in central contract repository with expiration reminders.

Ongoing Vendor Controls

- Quarterly review for high-risk vendors.
- SLAs and escalation paths documented in the contract.
- Access for vendor employees follows Tier 2/3 approval paths; vendor accounts are time-limited.

Travel Policy (Business Travel)

Booking and Approvals
- Travel must be pre-approved in the Travel Request form. Approvals require manager sign-off and travel budget confirmation.
- Preferred booking channels (partner travel portal) should be used for corporate rates and insurance coverage.

Expenses and Safety
- Employees are expected to follow lowest reasonable cost standards consistent with safety and schedule.
- Emergency travel deviations require post-hoc manager and finance approval.

Templates and Reference Forms

- Access Request (IT Portal): fields: requestor, resource, justification, tier, duration, manager, service owner.
- Purchase Request (Finance Form): fields: requestor, vendor, amount, budget center, quotes, approver chain.
- Vendor Risk Questionnaire (link): short-form and long-form variants.
- Travel Request Form: destination, dates, purpose, budget code, approver.

Example: Minimal Purchase Request JSON (copy into Purchase Request form if using API)

{
  "requestor": "name@example.com",
  "vendor": "Acme Cloud Services",
  "amount_usd": "7500",
  "budget_code": "ENG-OPS-2026",
  "justification": "Reserved capacity for Q2 load testing",
  "approvers": ["manager@example.com", "finance-approver@example.com"]
}

Governance & Exceptions

- Requests for policy exceptions must be submitted to the Control Owner via the Exception Request form and include compensating controls, risk assessment, and expiry date.
- Exceptions are reviewed monthly by a cross-functional panel (Security, Finance, Legal, Requesting Team).

Metrics and SLAs for the Hub

- Target approval times: Access Tier 1 = 24 hours, Tier 2 = 3 business days, Tier 3 = 5 business days.
- Procurement turnaround: <= 5 business days for <= $25k with complete docs.
- Vendor onboarding for high-risk vendors: target 30 days.

Operational Runbooks (Quick Links)

- Access: How to request access, how to recertify, emergency access escalation.
- Change: CAB scheduling, template for postmortem and rollbacks.
- Procurement: How to run an RFP and attach contracts.
- Vendor: Onboarding checklist and sample SLA contract clauses.

Retention and Audit

- All approvals, change tickets, vendor contracts, and travel approvals are retained per the retention catalog (default 7 years for contracts and financial artifacts; 3 years for routine change tickets).
- Audit logs for access and data access are stored in the centralized audit store with immutable retention.

How to Use This Hub

1. Start with the relevant template linked from the Templates section.
2. Follow the workflow steps and attach required artifacts.
3. If uncertain about risk classification, contact the Control Owner (Finance & Legal for procurement or Security for access).

Appendix: Quick Approval Matrix (human-readable)

- Low-risk access & purchases: manager-only approval.
- Medium-risk (service-impacting or > $1k): manager + functional approver.
- High-risk (PII/KMS or > $25k): manager + finance director + legal + security as applicable.

Contact and Escalation

- Finance & Legal (Control Owner for procurement): finance-legal@redwood.com
- Security (Control Owner for privileged access): security-ops@redwood.com
- Platform & IT (workflows & templates): platform-it@redwood.com
